summary: Ahead of Sunday's 191st Manchester derby, Erik ten Hag discusses goalkeeper André Onana, who Uefa's report described as a 'holding midfielder' for Inter in the Champions League final. Ten Hag wants him to be progressive but stresses pragmatism, saying the goalkeeper's main job is to save and that tactics depend on the opposition and team around him. The piece also covers Onana's rocky start after a £47.2m move, Bruno Fernandes's derby importance, and Ten Hag's view that Sir Jim Ratcliffe's pending investment is not a distraction.
one_line: Ten Hag says Onana should be progressive like an extra player but pragmatic, ahead of his Manchester derby debut against City.
key_facts: Erik ten Hag was asked whether André Onana can be the 'holding midfielder' Uefa's technical report described in his display for Internazionale in May's Champions League final.
Ten Hag says a keeper's main job is to save and guard his goal, but Onana can be used as an extra player and be more progressive, higher up the pitch.
Onana's last game for Inter was the 1-0 defeat by Manchester City in Istanbul, when City won their first Champions League and clinched the treble.
Onana, 27, will make his Manchester derby debut in Sunday's 191st derby, kicking off at 3.30pm.

Ten Hag says using the keeper as an extra man depends on the strength of the opposition's press and how good the team around him is; in his philosophy Onana has to do it every game, but it is not always possible.
Ten Hag wants United to be pragmatic and find a way to win even when not playing well.
United won their last three matches, against Sheffield United, Brentford and FC Copenhagen.
Onana was bought for £47.2m as a high-grade shot-stopper but had 'bombed', costing United goals and points, until impressing against Brentford and Copenhagen.
Ten Hag says English football differs in approach, speed, intensity and variety of styles, so players need time to adjust.
Last season's derby at Old Trafford ended 2-1 to United; Bruno Fernandes's equaliser was controversial as Marcus Rashford was offside but had not touched the ball.
Bruno Fernandes, the captain, has scored two goals in 12 United appearances this season.
Sir Jim Ratcliffe's bid to buy 25% of United for £1.3bn in return for control of football policy is expected to go through imminently.
Ten Hag does not think the club sale is a distraction, saying players are focused on the team and not strategic reviews or structures.
